extracted.intended_audience: federal agency officials (FOIA officers, program managers, compliance officers), legal counsel, and members of the public including FOIA requesters and persons with disabilities
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory standards governing (1) fees, fee waivers, advance payments, and payment procedures for FOIA requests to the Commission, and (2) enforcement of nondiscrimination on the basis of handicap (Section 504) including definitions, program accessibility, communications, self-evaluation, transition planning, and complaint procedures for agency programs and activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: FOIA fee categories and treatment for requesters
rubrics_metrics.description: Commission will provide documents to educational institutions for scholarly use (if request is from an educational institution) or non-commercial scientific research (if from a non-commercial scientific institution); representatives of the news media shall be provided documents for the cost of reproduction alone, excluding charges for the first 100 pages; all other requesters may be charged fees which recover the full reasonable direct costs of searching for and reproducing records responsive to the request, excluding the first 100 pages and first two hours of search time. Requests from record subjects for records about themselves are treated under the Privacy Act and permit fees only for reproduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains different fee treatments for educational/scientific requesters, news media, record subjects, and 'all other' requesters; highlights the free first 100 pages and first two hours of search time where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of limited back copies at no charge
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission keeps on file a limited quantity of back copies of Executive Director’s Recommendations, Committee Reports, and Commission Memorandums of Actions and will attempt to fill specific requests from that supply at no charge until the supply is exhausted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once supply is exhausted, requested documents will be provided in accord with the fee schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: No charging when cost of collection equals or exceeds fee; minimum fee
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may not charge fees to any requester if the cost of collecting the fee would be equal to or greater than the fee itself. The minimum fee for the production of information will be $2.00 (over and above the first free 100 pages and 2 hours search time, where applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Freedom of Information Officer may provide documents without charge or at a reduced charge if disclosure is in the public interest (see public interest factors).

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors considered for public-interest fee waiver or reduction
rubrics_metrics.description: In deciding whether a fee waiver or reduction is justified, the Commission will consider: (i) whether the subject concerns 'the operations or activities of the Government'; (ii) whether the information is 'likely to contribute' to understanding of government operations or activities; (iii) whether disclosure will contribute to 'public understanding' by the general public; (iv) whether the contribution to public understanding is 'significant'; (v) the existence and magnitude of any commercial interest of the requester; and (vi) whether the magnitude of any identified commercial interest is sufficiently large compared with the public interest so that disclosure is 'primarily in the commercial interest of the requester.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the enumerated public-interest balancing factors the agency must weigh when considering waivers or reductions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior approval and advance deposit thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Where duplication, review or search charges are likely to exceed $25.00, the agency shall notify the requester of the estimated amount of fees unless the requester indicated willingness to pay that amount. If fees are likely to exceed $250.00, the Commission may require advance payment of the fee in whole or in part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a requester previously failed to pay or is in arrears, the Commission may require payment of the full amount owed and an advance payment of the estimated fees before processing a new or pending request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension of response time for fee estimate/approval
rubrics_metrics.description: The dispatch of any request for estimated fee approval or advance deposit shall suspend, until a reply is received by the Freedom of Information Officer, the period within which the Freedom of Information Officer must respond to a written request for information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notifying the requester of estimated fees pauses the statutory response clock until the requester replies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregation to prevent fee avoidance
rubrics_metrics.description: A requester may not file multiple requests at the same time, each seeking portions of a document(s), solely to avoid payment of fees. When the Commission reasonably believes a requester is attempting to break a request into a series of requests to evade fees, the Commission may aggregate such requests and charge accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows the agency to treat related/subdivided requests as one request for fee assessment purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment of FOIA fees: methods and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees charged a person for the production of information must be paid in full prior to release of the information. Payment shall be made by personal check, postal money order or bank draft on a bank in the United States, made payable to the order of the Treasurer of the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies acceptable payment instruments and that payment precedes release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of Section 504 regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: This part effectuates section 119 of the Rehabilitation, Comprehensive Services, and Developmental Disabilities Amendments of 1978, which amended section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 to prohibit discrimination on the basis of handicap in programs or activities conducted by Executive agencies or the United States Postal Service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes statutory authority and scope (programs/activities conducted by the agency).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application scope
rubrics_metrics.description: This part applies to all programs or activities conducted by the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies the covered programs/activities (executive agency-conducted programs, not federally assisted programs for some definitions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: auxiliary aids
rubrics_metrics.description: Auxiliary aids means services or devices that enable persons with impaired sensory, manual, or speaking skills to have an equal opportunity to participate in, and enjoy the benefits of, programs or activities conducted by the agency. Examples include readers, brailled materials, audio recordings, telecommunications devices, telephone amplifiers, TDDs, interpreters, notetakers, and written materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to determine what aids an agency must furnish to ensure effective access; see communications section that requires providing appropriate aids where necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: complete complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete complaint means a written statement that contains the complainant’s name and address and describes the agency’s alleged discriminatory action in sufficient detail to inform the agency of the nature and date of the alleged violation of section 504, and is signed by the complainant or an authorized representative. Complaints filed on behalf of classes or third parties shall describe or identify (by name, if possible) the alleged victims of discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets the minimal contents required for the agency to accept and process a complaint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: handicapped person (inclusive standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: Handicapped person means any person who has a physical or mental impairment that substantially limits one or more major life activities, has a record of such an impairment, or is regarded as having such an impairment. 'Physical or mental impairment' and 'major life activities' are defined and illustrative conditions are listed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides the statutory/regulatory tests and examples for who is protected (including being 'regarded as' having an impairment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: qualified handicapped person
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualified handicapped person is defined contextually: (1) for preschool/elementary/secondary education, a handicapped person who is a member of a class otherwise entitled to receive education services; (2) for programs requiring performance/accomplishment, a handicapped person who meets essential eligibility requirements and can achieve the purpose without program modifications that would fundamentally alter the program; (3) for other programs, a handicapped person who meets essential eligibility requirements for participation or receipt of benefits; (4) defined for employment in 29 CFR 1613.702(f) which applies by reference to § 457.140.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determines who must be afforded protections and when program modifications are required versus when they would constitute fundamental alteration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-evaluation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency shall, by August 24, 1987, evaluate its current policies and practices that do not or may not meet the requirements of this part, make necessary modifications, provide opportunity for interested persons (including handicapped persons or organizations) to participate by submitting comments, and maintain on file for three years a description of areas examined and any modifications made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates an agency internal review, public participation in that review, and public records of findings and changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency shall make available to employees, applicants, participants, beneficiaries, and other interested persons information regarding the provisions of this part and its applicability to the programs or activities conducted by the agency, and make such information available in such manner as the head of the agency finds necessary to apprise such persons of their protections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires proactive dissemination of information about rights and protections under these regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: General prohibitions against discrimination (broad nondiscrimination standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: No qualified handicapped person shall, on the basis of handicap, be excluded from participation in, be denied the benefits of, or otherwise be subjected to discrimination under any program or activity conducted by the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the overarching nondiscrimination mandate from which more specific prohibitions derive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific prohibitions in provision of aids, benefits, or services
rubrics_metrics.description: In providing any aid, benefit, or service, the agency may not, directly or through contractual/licensing/other arrangements, on the basis of handicap: (i) deny opportunity to participate or benefit; (ii) afford an opportunity that is not equal to that afforded others; (iii) provide an aid/benefit/service that is not as effective in affording equal opportunity to obtain the same result or benefit; (iv) provide different or separate aids/benefits/services to handicapped persons unless necessary to provide equally effective benefits; (v) deny opportunity to participate as a member of planning or advisory boards; (vi) otherwise limit enjoyment of any right, privilege, advantage, or opportunity enjoyed by others receiving the aid/benefit/service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates concrete ways discrimination may occur in program delivery and participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on discriminatory criteria, methods, site selection, procurement, and licensing
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency may not: (3) utilize criteria or methods of administration the purpose or effect of which would subject qualified handicapped persons to discrimination or defeat the objectives of a program; (4) in selecting the site or location of a facility, make selections the purpose or effect of which would exclude handicapped persons or defeat program objectives; (5) in selecting procurement contractors, use criteria that subject qualified handicapped persons to discrimination; (6) administer licensing or certification programs in a manner that subjects qualified handicapped persons to discrimination or establish requirements for licensees/certified entities that do so (though the programs/activities of licensed entities are not themselves covered).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers administrative, locational, procurement, and regulatory mechanisms that can have discriminatory effects and are therefore prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Most integrated setting requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency shall administer programs and activities in the most integrated setting appropriate to the needs of qualified handicapped persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directs agencies to favor inclusion and integration when delivering services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employment nondiscrimination procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: No qualified handicapped person shall, on the basis of handicap, be subjected to discrimination in employment under any program or activity conducted by the agency. The definitions, requirements, and procedures of section 501 of the Rehabilitation Act (29 U.S.C. 791), as established by the EEOC in 29 CFR part 1613, shall apply to employment in federally conducted programs or activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employment complaints/requirements are governed by EEOC procedures and regulations (29 CFR part 1613).

rubrics_metrics.name: Program accessibility for existing facilities (overall accessibility standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency shall operate each program or activity so that the program or activity, when viewed in its entirety, is readily accessible to and usable by handicapped persons. This does not necessarily require making each existing facility accessible, nor actions that would substantially impair a historic property or result in fundamental alteration or undue financial/administrative burdens (burden on agency to prove).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits alternative methods to achieve overall program accessibility; where changes would be a fundamental alteration or undue burden, the agency must document and adopt other measures to ensure handicapped persons receive benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods to achieve program accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency may comply through means such as redesign of equipment, reassignment of services to accessible buildings, assignment of aides to beneficiaries, home visits, delivery of services at alternate accessible sites, alteration of existing facilities, construction of new facilities, use of accessible rolling stock, or any other methods that make programs readily accessible and usable. Structural changes are not required where other effective methods achieve compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In choosing methods the agency shall give priority to those that offer programs and activities in the most integrated setting appropriate; alterations must meet Accessibility Act/Architectural Barriers Act requirements as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility in historic preservation programs
rubrics_metrics.description: In historic preservation programs, the agency shall give priority to methods that provide physical access; where physical alteration is not required because of preservation or burden exceptions, alternative methods include using audio-visual materials to depict inaccessible portions, assigning persons to guide handicapped persons into or through portions that cannot be made accessible, or adopting other innovative methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balances preservation concerns with access and lists acceptable alternative accommodations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time periods for compliance with program accessibility obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency shall comply with obligations under program accessibility by October 21, 1986, except that structural changes shall be made by August 22, 1989; in any event actions must be taken as expeditiously as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes deadlines for general and structural compliance milestones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition plan requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If structural changes will be undertaken, the agency shall develop, by February 23, 1987, a transition plan setting forth steps necessary to complete changes. The agency shall provide opportunity for interested persons to participate in development and shall make a copy available for public inspection. The plan shall, at minimum: (1) identify physical obstacles in facilities limiting accessibility; (2) describe in detail methods to make facilities accessible; (3) specify schedule for steps necessary to achieve compliance and, if plan period > 1 year, identify steps for each year; (4) indicate the official responsible for implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires planning, public participation, public availability, and concrete timelines and responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: New construction and alterations accessibility standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Each building or part of a building constructed or altered by, on behalf of, or for the use of the agency shall be designed, constructed, or altered so as to be readily accessible to and usable by handicapped persons. The definitions, requirements, and standards of the Architectural Barriers Act (42 U.S.C. 4151–4157), as established in 41 CFR 101–19.600 to 101–19.607, apply to buildings covered by this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates application of ABA standards for new builds and alterations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications: ensuring effective communication
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency shall take appropriate steps to ensure effective communication with applicants, participants, personnel of other Federal entities, and members of the public, including furnishing appropriate auxiliary aids where necessary to afford a handicapped person an equal opportunity to participate in and enjoy the benefits of a program or activity. In determining which auxiliary aid is necessary, the agency shall give primary consideration to the requests of the handicapped person. The agency need not provide individually prescribed devices, readers for personal use or study, or other devices of a personal nature. Where the agency communicates by telephone, TDDs or equally effective telecommunications shall be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Places emphasis on effective communication, deference to the individual's stated need, and reasonable limits (no obligation to provide personal devices).

rubrics_metrics.name: Information availability and signage
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency shall ensure that interested persons, including persons with impaired vision or hearing, can obtain information as to the existence and location of accessible services, activities, and facilities. The agency shall provide signage at a primary entrance to each of its inaccessible facilities, directing users to a location at which they can obtain information about accessible facilities, and shall use the international symbol for accessibility at each primary entrance of an accessible facility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires visible information and standard accessibility signage to guide users to accessible services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fundamental alteration/undue burden exception and agency burden of proof
rubrics_metrics.description: This part does not require the agency to take any action it can demonstrate would result in a fundamental alteration in the nature of a program or activity or in undue financial and administrative burdens. Where agency personnel believe proposed action would result in such alteration or burdens, the agency has the burden of proving that compliance would result in such alteration or burdens, the decision must be made by the agency head or designee after considering all agency resources, and must be accompanied by a written statement of reasons. If an action would result in such alteration or burdens, the agency shall take any other action that would not result in such alteration or burdens but would ensure handicapped persons receive benefits and services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets procedural and evidentiary requirements for invoking fundamental alteration/undue burden defenses, including a written justification and exploration of alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaint filing time limit and acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency shall accept and investigate all complete complaints for which it has jurisdiction. All complete complaints must be filed within 180 days of the alleged act of discrimination; the agency may extend this time period for good cause. If the agency receives a complaint over which it does not have jurisdiction, it shall promptly notify the complainant and make reasonable efforts to refer the complaint to the appropriate government entity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines timeliness and referral obligations for complaints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification to ATBCB for buildings subject to ABA
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency shall notify the Architectural and Transportation Barriers Compliance Board upon receipt of any complaint alleging that a building or facility that is subject to the Architectural Barriers Act of 1968 is not readily accessible to and usable by handicapped persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures interagency notification for complaints implicating ABA-covered facilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigation results, remedy, and appeal timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 180 days of receipt of a complete complaint for which it has jurisdiction, the agency shall notify the complainant of the results of the investigation in a letter containing: (1) findings of fact and conclusions of law; (2) a description of a remedy for each violation found; and (3) a notice of the right to appeal. Appeals of findings or remedies must be filed by the complainant within 90 days of receipt of the letter. The head of the agency shall process timely appeals and shall notify the complainant of the results of the appeal within 60 days of receipt; if additional information is needed, the head has 60 days from receipt of the additional information to make a determination. Time limits in paragraphs (g) and (j) may be extended with permission of the Assistant Attorney General.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides concrete procedural deadlines for investigation, notification, appeals, and extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegation of investigative authority but not final determination
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency may delegate its authority for conducting complaint investigations to other Federal agencies, except that the authority for making the final determination may not be delegated to another agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits operational delegation while preserving final decision authority with the agency.
